Archival Dispatch: 16 Master Broadcasts Dated Across Abbott and Costello, Arch Oboler Horror, Spike Jones, and Airtime

Batch 64 Forensic Discoveries

Batch 64 resolves and dates 16 historical radio broadcasts spanning iconic vaudeville comedy routines, experimental radio horror, musical satire, military variety, and diplomatic jazz transmissions: Abbott and Costello's legendary 'Slowly I Turned (Niagara Falls Routine)' (October 19, 1944), 3 masterpieces of radio dread from visionary playwright Arch Oboler (including 'The Dark' and 'The Day the Sun Exploded' at the end of WWII), 2 musical slapstick satires from The Spike Jones Show (including his famous Nutcracker Suite parody), 4 crime and supernatural tales from Night Watch (1954), Gisèle MacKenzie and Skitch Henderson hosting jazz giant Cab Calloway on the Air Force Reserve's Airtime (1956), 3 State Department jazz preservation broadcasts from Notes on Jazz (featuring Louis Armstrong and Lionel Hampton), and Standard Oil's The Standard Hour.
